If you're criticizing, you don't count - a quote worth a pause.

Kevin Trudeau explains that to see the seed of a greater benefit in every problem, you have to cut back your judgment and criticism of others and of yourself.

He shares a quote he believes came from Roosevelt: it's not the critic who counts, not the one who points out how the strong man stumbles.

It's a blunt idea, and it's worth a moment of thought.

Do you criticize yourself more than you criticize anyone else?

#ad #mindset #success

Imagine never needing anyone to prove you right.

Kevin Trudeau paints a picture of being supremely confident without being arrogant. In it, you never need to be validated, never need to argue or debate, and never need to be recognized or given credit.

He adds total clarity and certainty while staying completely humble.

It is a picture of calm confidence to think about, not a promise of any result.

Which part of this picture appeals to you most?

#ad #mindset #confidence

Why do bad things happen to good people? Start here.

Kevin Trudeau says that when you see something happen in someone else's life, you can't know what is in their heart, what they want, or what has to play out for them.

So his first rule is simple: don't judge and don't criticize. He applies it to his own story too, asking whether you could know what he was asking for.

It's a thought worth sitting with before you react to anyone.

When did you last judge a situation before knowing the whole story?
